resources.string: Your pets\' devices, on your own server.
Shown in the panel\'s list of signed-in phones.
Plain HTTP: the password and the session travel unencrypted. Use it only on your home network.
This is not a server address.
Use an address that starts with https://.
HTTPS is required outside your home network.
No petkit-local server answers at this address. Check it, and the path of your reverse proxy if it has one.
This server has no password yet. Set one in the panel\'s “Phone app access” card, then sign in.
This server speaks version %1$d of the phone-app API and this app speaks version %2$d. Update petkit-local or the app.
Too many wrong passwords. Wait before trying again.
The server cannot be reached. Check the address and your connection.
The server ran into an error. Try again later.
The server ran into an error (HTTP %1$d). Try again later.
Your server is on your home network. Android asks you to allow this app to reach devices on the local network, without which it cannot reach the server.
Local network access was refused, so the app cannot reach a server on your home network. Allow it in this app\'s Android settings, or use an HTTPS address reachable from the internet.
You were signed out: this phone\'s session was revoked in the panel, the password was changed, or it went unused for 90 days.
You were signed out: the password was removed in the panel. Set a new one there to sign in again.
